questions.model: I did not measure it myself. An agency or a book did. So it is secondary.

questions.q: Give one limitation of a flood risk map.
questions.a: It shows likelihood, not certainty; may be out of date; broad scale

questions.q: How could rainfall records help explain your infiltration results?
questions.a: Wet soil from recent rain slows infiltration

questions.q: Find your area on the flood risk map and one river level gauge near you (or use the example sheet). In the portal response box, describe what each shows and link it to your hypotheses.
questions.a: Two sources described accurately and linked to H1 or H2
questions.model: Teacher models the flood risk map for the school's example postcode.

questions.q: (4 marks, own exam-style) Assess the reliability of one secondary source you used.
questions.a: Strengths (official, consistent methods) and limits (model, scale, gaps), with a judgement

questions.q: How could secondary data show whether your fieldwork day was typical?
questions.a: Compare rainfall that week with long-term averages

questions.q: Big question: what can official data tell you?
questions.a: Wider and longer patterns, such as flood risk and river response, that give context
